calendar.impact: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 lands against an API print of a 9.0 million barrel crude build and a 1.5 million barrel distillate build; distillate stocks at 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, are the line that matters. The exchange figures are the Abu Dhabi round's only dated deliverable.
calendar.title: EIA weekly petroleum report, 12:00 p.m. ET (delayed for Veterans Day); Abu Dhabi prisoner-exchange final numbers due

calendar.impact: Enbridge flagged on its Nov 6 call that producers and governments could resolve the negotiations by Nov 15, carried as a soft target the CEOs may extend. Alberta's Pacific Link royalty incentives, expected later this month, are the provincial leg of the same file. No terms are announced and no volumes are committed.
calendar.title: Possible producer and government announcement on pipelines, production growth and GHG abatement

calendar.impact: The deadline for December shipper nominations. The registered December judgment call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows the close, with the balance showing roughly 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space into the notice and December still without a trade after five sessions.
calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close

calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the fourth quarter capacity review setting the baselines for 2027 quotas. The November monthly report leaves demand growth unchanged and prints October DoC production at 41.23 million barrels a day on secondary sources.
calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework

changes.balance: The strip's November tightening now has two traded wider sessions against it, and the second came with both legs of the export spread voting the same way, which a single-leg move would not prove. December's missing fact is still a trade: five sessions of marks, the last of them flat, carry no information the nominations close will not force into the open on Nov 17.
changes.body: The Nov 11 ICE file gives the strip's turn a second traded day. January WCS is -$24.85 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 11), wider by $0.45 on 500 lots, after Tuesday's 895-lot widening ended the four-session tightening run. The deferred traded tenors widened in smaller size (July through September on 120 lots each, October and November on 180 each) and February through June marked unchanged on zero lots. December is -$28.49, unchanged on zero lots: a fifth straight session without a December trade, with the run of marked tightenings stalled at flat. Houston's January matched TMW's January lot for lot, 500 lots wider by $0.50 to -$17.50, with February and March wider by $0.50 on 200 lots each. The rest of the December complex did not move at all.
changes.conditional: A third traded wider session in January, or December's first trade printing wider, confirms the strip has turned into the nominations close; a return to traded tightening on comparable volume reopens the November trend and leaves the two wider days as a position wash.
changes.delta: TMW Jan27 -$24.85 (-$0.45, 500 lots, after 895 wider lots Tuesday); Dec26 -$28.49 (unchanged, 0 lots, fifth straight session without a trade); ARV Jan27 -$17.50 (-$0.50, 500 lots); ARV Dec26 -$18.97 (0 lots). ARV to TMW: December +$9.53, January +$7.35. December WCS outright $58.04 on Wednesday's WTI settle of $86.53. TMR Dec +$0.58, TMS Dec +$8.48, TMF Dec +$9.17, TMU Dec +$4.75, each unchanged on zero lots.
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 11, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 10, 2026
changes.title: January WCS widened a second straight traded session and Houston matched it lot for lot, while December completed five sessions without a trade

changes.balance: Flat price is trading headlines in both directions inside a two-day round trip while the dated supply facts accumulate on one side: OPEC+ output up in October, an API build awaiting grading, and a Canadian balance still tanking about 200 kb/d a month. The curve's shape (backwardation flattening, latest dated analysis Nov 9) is the steadier read than either session's settle.
changes.body: Wednesday's session rose nearly 3 percent intraday and settled with roughly half the gain, and Thursday's Asian session reversed the settle entirely. The factors on the board for the up move are live Hormuz incident flow, Tehran's on-record denial of negotiations, the Russian refining campaign and positioning after a 13 to 16 percent weekly fall; against it stand the OPEC monthly's October production increase and the API build, which landed after the settle. The monthly report leaves 2026 demand growth unchanged at 180 kb/d and 2027 at 2.55 million barrels a day, leaves non-OPEC+ supply growth unchanged, and prints a Saudi production gap of about 1.37 million barrels a day between the kingdom's direct communication (10.563) and secondary sources (9.194), with the independent surveys near the secondary figure. OPEC's own estimate has global inventories down 537 million barrels from a February peak to 8.043 billion at end-September.
changes.conditional: If today's inventory report confirms the API build in size, the oversupply side of the board gains its first official print of the week; a draw against the API reopens the tightening read and leaves the MOMR production jump as an October fact the November flows have yet to repeat.
changes.delta: Brent Jan27 settled $92.76 (+$1.27, +1.4 percent) and WTI Dec26 $86.53 (+$0.49, +0.6 percent) on Wednesday, off intraday highs near $94.26 and $88.31; by 0426 GMT Thursday Brent was $91.29 (-$1.47) and WTI $85.29 (-$1.24), WTI below Tuesday's two-month-low settle; Brent to WTI $6.23 at the settle, $6.00 in Asia. MOMR: DoC crude production +2.04 Mb/d in October to 41.23 Mb/d (secondary sources); Saudi direct communication 10.563 Mb/d against 9.194 secondary; 2026 demand growth unchanged at +180 kb/d to 105.72 Mb/d.
changes.source: Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 11, 2026; Reuters, Nov 12, 2026; OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report, Nov 11, 2026
changes.title: Wednesday's flat-price recovery round-tripped in Asia, and the OPEC monthly printed October OPEC+ output up 2.04 million barrels a day with demand growth unchanged
changes.vintage: Reuters and Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 11-12, 2026; OPEC MOMR, Nov 11, 2026

changes.balance: The diplomacy track has produced its testable item (a dated prisoner number) and nothing for the energy balance; the energy content of the week is in today's print and in the strike ledger, not in the communiques. A confirmed distillate build eases the one tight leg the cracks are priced on; another draw extends it.
changes.body: The Abu Dhabi round's only deliverable is humanitarian: both delegation heads and the US mediators confirm a large-scale prisoner exchange in principle, with the final numbers to be determined today. Russia's foreign minister put the sequencing on the record: no ceasefire before the future security architecture is settled. The offered truce at sea and on energy targets has had no Russian reply in the primary reporting, and the strike ledger continued through the talks and after them: Ust-Luga's substation fire on Nov 11 with no loading impact reported, Kirishi unassessed, and eight Ukrainian regions hit overnight Nov 11-12. Today's inventory report grades the API's build set (the opposite-signed version that circulated Wednesday was editor-corrected to the same build set) against distillate stocks at a 22-year low.
changes.conditional: Publication of the final exchange figures today confirms the round's one real item; any Russian answer to the sea and energy truce, in either direction, is the first energy content of the round and reopens the flow read.
changes.delta: Trilateral ended after two days: prisoner exchange agreed in principle (1,000 to 1,500 per side by speaker; final numbers due Nov 12); no ceasefire, no territory or guarantees agreement, no joint statement, no next-round date; Kyiv's sea and energy truce offer unanswered; Russia attacked eight Ukrainian regions overnight Nov 11-12. EIA w/e Nov 6 report today 12:00 p.m. ET: API crude +9.0 Mbbl, distillate +1.5, gasoline flat, Cushing +0.182, SPR -2.7 to 279.5 on the API count; standing official distillate stocks 99.3 Mbbl, lowest since May 2003; diesel crack $91.43 validated Nov 12.
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 11-12, 2026; AP, Nov 11, 2026; EIA release schedule, Nov 12, 2026
changes.title: Abu Dhabi ended with a prisoner exchange agreed in principle and no ceasefire, and the delayed inventory report lands today at noon ET
changes.vintage: Reuters and AP, Nov 11-12, 2026; EIA release schedule, checked Nov 12, 2026

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. The registered December judgment call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack now includes the balance build with November and December supply running about 192 and 216 kb/d above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a January differential that has printed two traded wider sessions (895 lots, then 500, with Houston's January matching the second lot for lot), a December front month that has not traded in five sessions, and a Brent to WTI spread at $6.23 keeping the export leg shut. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows the close and grades the call. A possible producer and government announcement on pipelines, production growth and GHG abatement around Nov 15 sits in front of the close.
flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, the balance shows about 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop before the nominations close

flags.body: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. The API bulletin for the week ending Nov 6 printed a distillate build of 1.5 million barrels and a crude build of 9.0 million against a survey expectation near a 1.0 million draw; the opposite-signed version that circulated on Wednesday was editor-corrected to this build set. The validated diesel crack is $91.43 on the Nov 12 print, priced for tightness. The EIA report lands today at 12:00 p.m. ET, delayed a day for Veterans Day: a confirmed distillate build is the first loosening signal against the stocks position, and another draw leaves the tight fact standing alone.
flags.title: Today's inventory report grades an API build against distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003
flags.trigger: The EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending Nov 6, released Nov 12 at 12:00 p.m. ET

flags.body: The trilateral ended Nov 11 with a large-scale prisoner exchange agreed in principle and the final numbers to be determined Nov 12. There is no ceasefire, no agreement on territory or security guarantees, and no date for a next round; Russia's position on the record is that the security architecture is settled before any ceasefire. Kyiv's offered truce at sea and on energy targets has had no Russian reply in the primary reporting. The strike ledger ran through the talks: Ust-Luga's substation fire Nov 11 with no loading impact reported, Kirishi unassessed since Nov 9, Russian refining capacity estimated down about 30 percent since late October by industry sources, and eight Ukrainian regions hit overnight Nov 11-12. In the Gulf, a fresh UKMTO warning (202-26) covers a Nov 11 tanker incident in the strait, with at least 10 ships hit in the first 10 days of November; AIS-visible crossings were 9 on Nov 11, a floor gauge, while flow estimates put Gulf crude exports at 80 to 85 percent of pre-war including pipelines and products at 35 to 40 percent.
flags.title: Abu Dhabi's energy content is an unanswered truce offer; the prisoner-exchange numbers due today are the round's only dated test
flags.trigger: Publication of the final prisoner-exchange figures, any Russian answer to the sea and energy truce offer, or a tier-1 flow read (TankerTrackers, CENTCOM) dated after Nov 11
